correctness.rationale: For a retained cell, the number of removed neighbours equals its deleted-row count plus its deleted-column count. In the same-parity case fewer than \(\min(m,n)\) omissions leave an untouched row and column with an even-degree retained intersection. At the sharp threshold, a rectangle has one omission in each shorter-direction row; a square must have all rows or all columns hit. With one omission per row, any nonfull column must receive an even number of omissions; full columns yield the odd-width special case. Thus even widths admit exactly even-fibre maps, odd widths exactly a full column. A square is the disjoint union with transposes, except the one-cell degeneracy. Multinomial enumeration gives \(m![x^m](\cosh x)^n\), and maximal number of used columns gives the correct leading asymptotic. Exhaustive adjacency-based enumeration agrees on every maximizing vertex subset in seventeen finite cases, but is not used as the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Ai et al. prove a lower bound for maximum degree at most four; their inspected full text gives no unrestricted rectangular-rook optimizer enumeration. Zeng and Guo et al. study broad existence/lower bounds; their abstracts do not imply an exact number of optimum rook-graph subsets, but their full texts were not available for a definitive exclusion. A result giving just a universal lower bound does not imply our exact equality-case count.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier scalar maximum is logically weaker: it certifies a size and one achieving construction but permits additional maximizers. The new proof rules out all other deletions and counts all even-fibre assignments and transposes. For instance the prior cardinality formula alone cannot yield the \(80\) different optimum subsets on a four-by-four board. Claims of absolute priority are not made.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An induced vertex set of a rook graph is equivalent to an edge set of a complete bipartite graph whose line graph has all induced degrees odd. For a retained edge, its line-graph degree is the sum of retained endpoint degrees minus two. Direct formulation and this line-graph reduction were searched. The known rook-graph formula gives only a numerical maximum, not classification of edge deletions with even column fibres.

originality.rationale: The June 24, 2026 public rook-graph question and accepted response completely cover the scalar optimum but do not classify or count the optimum vertex subsets. New content is a necessary-and-sufficient equality characterization, an even-fibre exponential generating function and its parity-dependent growth, none of which follows from the scalar size without additional structural work. The accessible 2025 primary full-text paper addresses a bounded-degree universal lower bound; two 2026 general results describe lower bounds rather than this equality enumeration in their accessible abstracts, but their uninspected bodies remain a bibliographic risk. Mathematical record, alias and accessible own-history queries found no matching counts; absence of hits alone is not evidence of novelty.

value.rationale: A natural open follow-up to a settled extremal size is a full classification of the optimizers and their multiplicity. The optimizer families bifurcate by shorter-side parity: exactly \(n\) extremizers for fixed odd m<n, versus an even-fibre count polynomial of degree \(m/2\) and leading coefficient \((m-1)!!\) for fixed even m<n. The counts exhibit substantially different combinatorial degeneracy and permit exact uniform sampling from optimizers. This is a nontrivial equality-case structure on all rectangular rook graphs, not a recomputation of the previously known cardinality.
